lots.guide_summary: All evidence is SOLD at Gowans, but none is the same item. The only vase that sold intact was a larger, plainer cream-ground modern vase at $125 hammer; a damaged small cobalt Moorcroft in a mixed lot made $55; small Moorcroft dishes and bowls make $55 to $120. No UNSOLD or ASKING entries found (eBay and the specialist sites are closed to us). All AUD, no currency conversion.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD entry (cobalt Orchid vase of this size) survives, so both maximum bids are 0 under the rules. For reference only: if the $125 cream vase were accepted as a comparable, keep would be 125/1.198 = 104.3, so $100, and flip would be (125 less 13% fees $16 less $12 post = $97)/2.396 = 40.5, so $40. The probable base crack argues for staying well under those figures.
lots.confidence_reason: Maker mark is read (impressed MOORCROFT) and the pattern is clear, but there is no same-item SOLD evidence and the base shows a probable hairline crack.
lots.condition: Body glaze bright, no chips seen on rim or body in the one side view. Base glaze crazed all over, and one darker, wider meandering line about 2cm long runs through the crazing on the inner base; enlarged it looks like a hairline or firing crack rather than crazing. Rest of the body not seen (only one side photographed).
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: squat cobalt vase with tube-lined orchid flowers, lot tag 195. Photo 2 (enlarged): impressed MOORCROFT with blue glaze run into the letters, a second blue smudge at lower right, crazed base, and a dark meandering line in the centre of the base that stands out from the crazing.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the dark line on the inside of the base a crack that goes through (does it ring true when tapped, any line visible inside the vase)? Are there any chips, restorations or other cracks on the back that is not photographed? Is there any other mark or signature on the base besides MOORCROFT?
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped outright. Researcher's $125 vase kept but rated close rather than a basis for a bid (different pattern, ground and size, photos checked). Framed Moorcroft prints, books and the chipped $2 mug and dish ignored as a different product or condition. Extra Gowans searches 'moorcroft orchid', 'orchid vase' and 'moorcroft pansy' found nothing beyond this lot; Grays search returned no usable result.

lots.guide_summary: One SOLD same-item entry: an identical plain concave 925 cuff of 26.9g made $80 hammer at Gowans in February 2026. Category guides (other sterling bangles and cuffs sold at Gowans, all SOLD) run $40 to $90, about $2.4 to $3.0 per gram. No UNSOLD or ASKING entries. All AUD. Melt floor (note only): silver about A$84.64/oz bid per the Perth Mint figure recorded by a sibling check today (7 Oct 2026; I could not re-read it, Perth Mint's page returned no price to curl and goldprice.org's feed was Forbidden), about A$2.72/g fine, so sterling about A$2.52/g: a 27g cuff is about A$68 melt, 35g about A$88.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD $80 / 1.198 = 66.8, rounded down to $65 (all-in $77.87). Flip: likely resale $90 (the $80 hammer plus a little for current higher silver), less about 13% selling fees ($11.70) and $10 tracked postage = $68.30; 68.30 / 2.396 = 28.5, rounded down to $25. If the cuff weighs well over 27g, melt rises (about $2.52/g) but the bid rules stay on the SOLD price until weight is confirmed.
lots.confidence_reason: 925 stamp read in the photos and one well-matched SOLD entry whose page and photos I checked; weight unknown and only one same-item sale.

lots.question_for_gowans: What does the cuff weigh in grams? Any other mark besides 925 (maker or country)?

lots.guide_summary: All SOLD, all Gowans, all in the last 10 months. Bundles of the same mid-century Tasmanian labels have made anything from $10 (11 labels incl Stork and Top, Aug 2026) to $440 (16 labels incl Haven, Sep 2026) and $450. Most ordinary bundles land $14 to $60 hammer (median about $40); four lots since mid-August made $280 to $450, which looks like two or more keen collectors bidding on particular lots rather than a reliable level, because $10 to $30 results happened in the same weeks. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence found. All AUD.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD is $10 (lot 434560, 11 similar labels, 2026-08-30): 10 / 1.198 = 8.3, rounded down to $5. Flip: likely resale about $40 (median of ordinary bundles), less about 13% fees ($5.20) and $10 postage = $24.80; 24.80 / 2.396 = 10.4, rounded down to $10. The $280 to $450 results are real sales but too lot-specific and volatile to set a bid on; anyone wanting to chase them is gambling on the same collectors turning up.
lots.confidence_reason: Labels read clearly in the photos and many matching SOLD entries opened with photos checked, but prices are wildly inconsistent ($10 to $450) so the value is not predictable.
lots.condition: Labels look clean, bright and unused with sharp colours; minor edge creases possible, backs not shown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Five photos show about 14 face-up labels with a few stacked beneath (Beautiful Isle at least doubled, possibly Top). Brands and packers read: Ideal Pears and Golden Key (W.D. Peacock), Boomerang, Haven, Beautiful Isle, Top Flite, Pinnacle (H. Jones & Co), Huonery (Port Huon Fruitgrowers Co-op), Bright Star (T.E. Butler), Top (Tasmanian Orchardists & Producers), Stork (Clements & Marshall), A. Port Pty Ltd, Tas Fruit Cat. 1 (later, plainer).
lots.question_for_gowans: How many labels are in the lot in total, and are there duplicates or extra labels under the top layer? Any tears, stains or trimmed edges?
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher's $100 lot 389454 (BOX OF APPLE & PEAR LABELS, 0 bids yet a sale price) and $35 lot 421354 (Peacock, 0 bids) dropped: a sale price with no bids suggests a post-auction or vendor deal, not a contested hammer. $100 lot 425991 (APPLE CASE LABELS ETC) dropped as unseen and 'etc' contents unknown. Researcher's summary omitted the low recent results ($10, $14, $15, $30); I added them from the same opened API pages. Researcher's 'Huon' label is actually 'Huonery' brand.
